issues.display_title: Issue #936: feat(editor): Closed room logo visibility — per-Information toggle, labelType-independent rendering, 3D roof logo (#934)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-936.mp4

Source PRD: #934 · PRD file: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-09-03-closed-room-logo-visibility/prd.md (branch product-docs) · Builds on #735 / #816

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

A Closed room's logo is decided by two different rules today. The 2D canvas draws it whenever the linked Information has a logo (closedRoomLogos → editor/draw.ts). The map, preview, live and embed overlays draw it only when that Information's labelType is "logo" (resolveMarkerRender → resolveLabelRender), which is why the Closed room toolbar's Add/Replace Logo forces labelType: "logo" onto a record that may be shared with points, areas and search results. There is no way to keep a logo on the record and not paint it on the room; the Room height slider still shows for a Closed room even though #816 made its height meaningless; and the editor's own Three.js 3D view (scene3d.ts) draws no Closed room logo at all — the roof logo from #816 lives on the MapLibre 3D map only.

Scope

  • Data — Information.showLogoInClosedRoom?: boolean. undefined means on, so existing records keep their logos; no migration. Information records ride the canvasData blob, so nothing changes on the backend.
  • One rule — closedRoomLogos becomes info.logo && info.showLogoInClosedRoom !== false; resolveMarkerRender applies the same rule to a Closed room anchor (fitHalf / logoTooSmall) instead of reading labelType, so the editor map, preview, live /v/[key] and embed overlays agree with the 2D canvas. Off → the ordinary room text label, never the fixed logo chip. Non-Closed rooms and every other object keep their labelType behaviour.
  • Closed room toolbar (SelectionToolbars.tsx) — hide the Room height slider when the selected room is Closed, leaving the stored height alone; keep type, colour and Add/Replace Logo; add a compact On/Off toggle that shows only when the linked Information has a logo and writes showLogoInClosedRoom. Upload/replace sets it true and no longer forces labelType: "logo" onto an existing record (the record the upload creates from scratch may still default to it).
  • Information modal Media tab — the same toggle beside Upload/Replace logo, shown only when form.logo exists; upload sets showLogoInClosedRoom: true; Remove hides the toggle.
  • Editor 3D view (scene3d.ts) — paint the Closed room logo on the room roof: logoFitBox bounds, contain-fit, aspect preserved, clear of the walls, skipped gracefully when the image fails to load or the room is too small.

Out of scope

  • Per-room visibility (the flag belongs to the Information record), logo cropping/placement, any backend endpoint, and changes to icon/photo/pano/text labels on other objects — PRD §2 non-goals.
  • LOGO_PAD_RATIO (how much of the roof the logo fills) stays as is — separate call, already noted on #816.

Acceptance

  • showLogoInClosedRoom survives save → reload; a record with a logo and no flag still shows the Closed room logo
  • showLogoInClosedRoom: false hides the room-sized logo on the 2D canvas, editor 3D view, editor map, preview, live and embed; the room shows its text label instead
  • Closed room toolbar: no Room height slider for a Closed room and the stored height is unchanged; type, colour and Add/Replace Logo remain; the toggle appears only once a logo exists
  • Toolbar upload/replace turns visibility on without changing an existing record's labelType
  • Media tab shows and saves the toggle beside Logo; upload turns visibility on; Remove hides the toggle
  • A Closed room whose Information has a logo but labelType: "text" still shows the logo on the map — the rule no longer reads labelType
  • Editor 3D view renders the logo on the roof, contain-fit inside logoFitBox, aspect preserved, not touching the walls
  • Points, shapes, safety, access, non-Closed rooms and ordinary label styles unchanged
  • Unit + component tests per PRD §6 (closedRoom, object-markers, MapObjectMarkers, SelectionToolbars, MediaTab); pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

RESULT

PR #937 → development, merge d617660, work commit 3de1cfb. 10 files + 1 new test file, +283 / −53.

Root cause — two rules decided the room-sized logo. The 2D canvas (closedRoomLogos → editor/draw.ts) drew it whenever the record had a logo; the map/preview/live/embed overlay (resolveMarkerRender → resolveLabelRender) only when labelType === "logo", so the toolbar upload forced that style onto a shared record. The Three.js editor view (scene3d.ts) had no Closed-room handling at all — the roof logo from #816 lives on the MapLibre map only.

Fix — Information.showLogoInClosedRoom? (unset = on, rides canvasData, no backend change). closedRoomLogoOn() is the one rule, read by closedRoomLogos and by resolveMarkerRender for Closed room anchors instead of labelType; off → text label, never the chip. Toolbar: Room height hidden for a Closed room, Show switch beside Replace Logo once a logo exists, upload turns it on without touching labelType. Media tab: the same switch, upload turns it on. Editor 3D: logo laid on the roof inside logoFitBox, contain-fit (containFit), texture cached per URL, failed load = no logo; the Closed colour is painted in that view now too, so the logo has ground.

Verified — 12 new tests, red first (closedRoom, object-markers, SelectionToolbars.closedRoom, MediaTab). pnpm test 2127 pass, lint 0 errors, tsc clean on src/. Browser probe on a scratch copy: upload → on; off drops the logo from 2D, 3D roof and map without reload; on → back; map roof logo survives the record's label style being set to Text.

Demo — .playwright-mcp/demo/936/video-936.mp4, 163 s, 1920×1080, 60 fps GPU. Beats: ordinary room → Closed (Height gone) → Add Logo (plan, 3D roof, switch) → off/on → record modal (Label: Text, Media switch) → map still painted.

Noticed, not in scope — Add Logo on a Closed room with no Information record yet (addInformation + setAreaInfo write canvasData) drops the room selection; the toolbar vanishes until the room is clicked again, data is right. The #816 demo passed this path on 26 Aug, so it regressed since. Own task if wanted.

issues.display_title: Issue #940: Bind project visibility to the update API and render a private state on /v/{key}
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-933-project-privacy.mp4

Source issue: #933 · Design issue: #932 · Backend counterpart: GoThruMedia/Gothru-3d-Floormap-API-GO#168

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Project visibility does not exist anywhere today. Project (src/actions/projects.ts:25-52) has no visibility field, updateProject (:131-144) accepts none, and the only thing resembling a privacy control is the publish/unpublish pair — which is a different axis: publish decides whether a live link exists at all, visibility decides who may follow it. /v/[key] renders one string, "This project is not available." (src/app/v/[key]/page.tsx:70), for a missing key, an unpublished project and a network failure alike, so there is nothing to build a restricted state out of.

This task wires the frontend to the is_public field API-GO#168 adds. It is blocked on that ticket — PATCH /v1/projects/:id drops unknown keys silently, so the toggle would appear to work and persist nothing.

Scope

  • Contract — is_public?: boolean on Project (absent on older payloads → treat as public, matching the backend's DEFAULT TRUE). updateProject's data gains isPublic?: boolean.

  • Toggle — a Public / Private item in the dashboard project "…" menu (ProjectViews.tsx), beside the existing Publish / Unpublish, with a handleVisibilityToggle in useDashboard.ts shaped like handlePublishToggle: optimistic flip on projects + recent, restoreProjectAt on failure, refreshList() in finally. Unlike publish it needs no confirm dialog — it is reversible and destroys nothing. Shown at every status; it only has an observable effect once the project is published, which the menu copy says.

  • Access state — getLiveFloorplanAction returns a discriminated result instead of unknown | null, so 403 (private) and 404/network (unavailable) stop collapsing into the same null:

    export type LiveFloorplanResult =
  | { ok: true; data: unknown }
  | { ok: false; reason: "private" | "unavailable" }

    /v/[key]/page.tsx gains a "private" status rendering "This project is private." in the same centred slot as the existing message. /embed/[key] re-renders that same component, so it inherits the state for free.

  • Metadata leak — v/[key]/layout.tsx:59-74 fetches the live blob in generateMetadata and titles the page saved?.projectName. A branch added only to page.tsx would still ship a private project's real name to every crawler and link unfurler, plus a canonical URL and an OG image probe. On reason: "private" the layout must fall back to the "MapThru" title and /og.png, emit no canonical, and set robots: { index: false, follow: false }. src/app/sitemap.ts enumerates no projects, so there is no second leak there.

  • Analytics — reportIndoorMapOpened's outcome union (src/lib/analytics/viewerEvent.ts:34) gains "restricted", so a deliberate privacy block stops being counted as a broken load.

AC3 — Google Blue Line

Grep over the whole tree for blue.?line|street.?view|streetview|gsv returns exactly one hit: prose in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-18-billing-feature-gating-ecosystem-design.md:13. There is no Blue Line trigger in this repo, so #933's third criterion is a non-regression requirement, not a build.

Honoured by keeping previewNavbarSlots (src/lib/collaboration/previewNavbar.ts:26) a function of (caps, status) only — visibility must never become a parameter, or a private project would start hiding publish controls. That function has no test file today; this task adds one to pin it.

Out of scope

  • The fuller visibility UI of #932 — a selector in the project header and settings panel, status badges, and the informational note that visibility is independent of Blue Line publishing. This task ships the binding and the guest-facing state; #932 ships the design.
  • Any change to /api/live/[key]/file and /image (route.ts:33-35): both mirror upstream status verbatim, so API-GO#168's gate on live_get.go covers them with no frontend diff.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Toggling Public → Private in the dashboard menu PATCHes isPublic and survives a reload; the row/tile reflects it optimistically and rolls back on failure
  • Publish and Unpublish still work on a private project, and toggling visibility never changes status — the two axes stay independent
  • A guest opening a private project's /v/{key} sees "This project is private."; a public published project is unchanged
  • /embed/{key} shows the same restricted state
  • An unknown or unpublished key still shows "This project is not available." — private and missing are distinct states
  • generateMetadata for a private key emits the "MapThru" title, /og.png, no canonical, and robots: index: false — the project name never reaches a crawler
  • indoor_map_opened reports outcome: "restricted" for a private project, not "unavailable"
  • previewNavbarSlots takes no visibility parameter, with a test pinning it (AC3)
  • Existing tests updated for the new getLiveFloorplanAction shape (src/actions/__tests__/projects.test.ts:183-225, src/app/v/[key]/__tests__/metadata.test.ts), plus a private case in each
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

RESULT

PR #941 → development (f6e7c8c), release PR #942 → main (5379740, Deploy workflow green). Work commit ed6e1e5. 9 files, +293 / −26.

Shipped — Project.is_public (absent → public) and updateProject accepts isPublic. A Make Private / Make Public item in the dashboard "…" menu: no confirm dialog, and the menu stays open so the label flips in place and a failed write, which snaps it back, is seen. The flag has one reader, so the state lives in the menu instead of being drilled through the tile, the row and the dashboard's list state.

getLiveFloorplanAction returns {ok: true, data} | {ok: false, reason: "private" | "unavailable"} — a bare null collapsed private and missing into one answer. /v/{key} renders "This project is private."; /embed/{key} re-renders the same component and inherits it. generateMetadata is gated too: crawlers run with JS off and see only the head, so a private key now emits the MapThru title, /og.png, no canonical and robots: noindex — a branch in page.tsx alone would still have shipped the project's real name to every link unfurler. indoor_map_opened reports outcome: "restricted".

AC3 — no Blue Line trigger exists in this repo (one grep hit, prose in a spec), so it is a non-regression requirement: previewNavbarSlots stays a function of (capabilities, publish status) alone, now pinned by a test where it had none.

Verified — pnpm test 2140 pass / 228 files, tsc --noEmit clean, pnpm lint 0 errors. New: ProjectVisibility.test.tsx (5), previewNavbar.test.ts (5); projects.test.ts and metadata.test.ts updated with a private case each. One branch is deliberately untested and says so in the file — the catch path when the action throws: React re-dispatches a handler error through a synthetic DOM event, jsdom turns that into window.onerror, and vitest fails the test even though the component catches it (confirmed with a probe). The rejected-result case covers the identical revert.

Demo — .playwright-mcp/demo/933/video-933-project-privacy.mp4, 89 s, 1920×1080, 60 fps GPU. Beats: share link from the dashboard menu → Make Private (label flips, Unpublish untouched) → the same link shows "This project is private." → Make Public → the map is back. Ran against the live backend; the demo project was verified published / is_public = true afterwards.

Noticed, not in scope — the demo runner's clickEl drives real mouse coordinates and never scrolls, so a card below the fold is clicked at a point that is not on screen. Only findCard scrolls, as a side effect of its own clicks. Worked around in 933/scenario.mjs with scrollIntoViewIfNeeded; lib/overlay.mjs still has the sharp edge.

issues.display_title: Issue #945: feat(editor): object layer order actions on sidebar overlay rows (#943)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-945-object-layer-order.mp4

Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

PRD: #943 · Decisions: #944 (all five answered)
Repo: gothru-3d-floormap (frontend only — no backend work)

Layer-order actions on sidebar overlay rows in the 2D editor. Built to the decisions in #944, not to the literal PRD text — where they differ, #944 wins.

Decisions baked in

  • D1=B — ordering is within one object type only. To Front raises an object above others of its own type. A shape never goes above a marker; an Area never goes above a shape. PRD R3/R4 describe cross-type ordering and are superseded.
  • D2=B — the All list is sorted front-to-back, so it reads as the layer list. This replaces the newest-first sort.
  • D3 — there is no panorama object type. Imported panoramas are Points carrying a pano-linked Information record, so they are covered by "point". level.panoramas is dead (no production writer) — do not build against it.
  • D4=A — fix the access-marker undo gap as part of this work.
  • D5 — map view: "no visible change", verified by eye, not byte-identical output.

Scope

Supported rows: Areas (manual only), shapes (rect / circle / polygon), points, safety markers, access markers.
Not supported: walls, detected Rooms, doors, windows. These rows show no menu.

Why this is more than a menu

The 2D editor has no z-order model. redraw2D (src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/draw.ts:38) paints in fixed type bands; within one band, z is the array index. Under D1=B that is enough — reordering = splicing the object's own array — so no new stored field is needed and no painter rewrite is needed. That is the whole reason B is cheap.

Two things come free from that:

  • Persistence (R9). modelToLevel (src/lib/floorplanEditor/bridge.ts:386-410) maps points / safetyAnnotations / accessPoints / shapes 1:1 preserving array order, and layout.areas keeps manualAreas order. Nothing to add.
  • Undo (R10). snapshot() (src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/history.ts:10) already captures manualAreas, shapes, points, safety whole. Only access is missing — that is D4.

Build

1. Reorder helper — new pure module, e.g. src/lib/editor/layerOrder.ts.
toFront / toBack / forward / backward over (length, index) -> newIndex, plus a splice helper. Already-at-the-edge is a no-op (no error, no history step) — that answers the PRD's four "decide the edge behaviour" items uniformly.

2. Engine command — src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/commands.ts.
One entry point taking (kind, id, action). Resolve id → index in the owning model array, splice, then pushUndo before the mutation, and rebuild + notifyChange after. Follow the existing command shape in that file.

3. Selection index fixups — the main trap.
ctx.selShapes holds indices into model.shapes, and ctx.selManual is an index into model.manualAreas. A splice invalidates both, so a reorder with something selected will highlight the wrong object unless the indices are remapped. ctx.selAnnos is keyed by id and is safe.
Reordering manual Areas also shifts manualIndex, which recomputeRooms (src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/model-sync.ts:117) assigns by array position — so ctx.areaColors / ctx.areaLogos, keyed by room index, must be re-keyed after an Area reorder. areaMeta itself is keyed by area id (manualMetaKey) and survives untouched.

4. Access in the undo snapshot (D4).
Add access to snapshot() and to restore() in history.ts. Use ??, not || [], matching the note already in restore — snapshots persisted in localStorage before this key existed carry no access, and || [] would wipe every access marker on the first undo after deploy. This also fixes undo for ordinary access-marker edits, which has never worked.

5. Row menus — four components, not one.
ObjectSection.tsx:70 routes by role and filter, so the menu is needed in all of:

  • UnifiedObjectList — the All list, and every list for Viewers
  • SimpleAnnotationList — point / safety / rect / circle / polygon when canEdit
  • AccessList — access, both roles
  • EngineRoomList kind="area" — Areas when canEdit

Reuse the ActionsMenu pattern from src/components/dashboard/ProjectViews.tsx:141 (Popover + MENU_ITEM). There is no dropdown-menu.tsx primitive — only popover.tsx. Do not add a dependency. The trigger must not resize the row: fixed-size icon button, revealed on hover/focus, and stopPropagation on click so opening the menu does not select the row.
Menu is edit-only — Viewers see no order actions.

6. All sorted front-to-back (D2).
Replace sortNewestFirst in buildObjectRows (src/lib/editor/objectRows.ts:100) with a paint-order comparator: band descending, then array index descending within the band. Band order top→bottom is access, safety, point, shape, area, wall, window, door, room — read it off redraw2D, and leave a comment tying the two together so they cannot drift.
The per-type filtered lists need no sort change: their newestFirst prop already reverses the array, which under D1=B is already topmost-first.

7. Reset to All after an order action (R8).
filter is local state in ObjectSection. Lift it (or expose a setter) so the four row components can reset it. Reset fires only for the four order actions — not for select, delete, rename or any other row action.

Acceptance

  • Order menu on Area, shape, point, safety and access rows in every list that shows them; absent on wall, Room, door, window rows; absent for Viewers.
  • Four actions, labelled exactly To Front, To Back, Bring Forward, Bring Backward.
  • Each action moves only the row's object, even with several objects selected on the canvas.
  • Ordering is within the object's own type (D1=B).
  • An action at the edge does nothing and records no history step.
  • The 2D canvas and the sidebar both update immediately.
  • Using an order action from a filtered list returns the list to All.
  • All is ordered front-to-back and the row visibly moves after an order action.
  • Order survives save and reopen.
  • Undo reverses an order change, repeatedly, across several actions — including for access markers.
  • Selection stays on the same object after a reorder (indices remapped).
  • Closed-room colours and logos are unchanged after reordering an Area.
  • Walls, detected Rooms, doors and windows behave exactly as before.
  • No visible change to preview, live, embed, map or 3D view.

Tests

Unit: the reorder helper (all four actions, both edges, length 1); the paint-order comparator; the access undo round-trip. Component: menu present/absent per row type and per role, action calls the engine with the row's own id, filter resets to All.
pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm exec tsc --noEmit all green before review.

Follow-ups, not in this task

  • PRD #943 wording: R3/R4 and the acceptance checklist still describe cross-type ordering (D1=B supersedes); panorama-marker line (D3); "map view unchanged" → "no visible change" (D5).
  • All losing its newest-first order is a deliberate consequence of D2=B — see #944. If newest-first should return as a second sort option, that is its own task.

RESULT

All four sub-tasks are in #953, one PR to development.
9f577db #948 — access markers into the undo snapshot
77828a2 #949 — All ordered front-to-back
0f533aa #950 — engine command + selection remap
eaa16fb 779c849 #951 — the menu, and age-based row numbers
ad730ab 3D z-fighting on overlapping shapes (render-only)

Cheap because #944 D1=B scopes ordering to one type: the array index already IS the z, so a reorder is a splice, and persistence and undo come free.

For PM. The 3D fix is a per-shape polygonOffset — a depth bias only, nothing touches sh.height, the mesh position or any geometry. It makes the 3D panel agree with the 2D plan about which shape is on top. PRD non-goal 2 says the feature must not change 3D ordering; it does not add ordering there (the previous behaviour was undefined, not a different order) but the panel is now consistent instead of striped. Flagged, not decided. The map builds its own extrusions and can have the same coplanar overlap — not touched, worth its own task if it turns up.

pnpm test 2192 pass / 231 files · tsc --noEmit clean · pnpm lint 0 errors. Demo recorded at .playwright-mcp/demo/945/ (1920x1080, 60 fps).

issues.display_title: Issue #948: fix(editor): access markers are missing from the undo snapshot (#945)
issues.main_description_html:
Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Parent: #945 · PRD: #943 · Decisions: #944 (D4=A)

Access markers are missing from the editor's undo snapshot, so no change to an access marker has ever been undoable — not just reordering. #944 D4=A rules this fixed as part of the layer-order work. Standalone and independent of the other three tasks.

The bug

snapshot() in src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/history.ts:10 captures walls, doors, windows, icons, roomNames, manualAreas, scaleMmPerUnit, roomHeights, shapes, points, safety, areaMeta. model.access is not there, and restore() does not put it back. Ctrl+Z after adding, moving, retyping or deleting an access marker leaves the marker exactly as it was.

Build

Add access to snapshot(), and restore it in restore().

Use ??, never || []. restore already carries this rule for points / safety / areaMeta with a comment explaining it: undo stacks are mirrored to localStorage under fp_history:<level_id> and survive a deploy, so snapshots written before this key existed carry no access. || [] would wipe every access marker on the first undo after release.

Check whether noteStoreEdit (same file) should compare access too. It currently compares only points and safety — the kinds a store action writes behind the engine's back. src/lib/editor/access.ts writes access markers from the store, so this likely needs the same treatment; confirm against that file rather than assuming.

Acceptance

  • Add an access marker → Ctrl+Z removes it.
  • Move an access marker → Ctrl+Z returns it to the old position.
  • Change an access marker's type → Ctrl+Z restores the old type.
  • Delete an access marker → Ctrl+Z brings it back, with its accessId group intact.
  • Redo works for each of the above.
  • A history entry persisted before this change (no access key) restores without wiping existing access markers.
  • Cross-floor access groups still resolve after an undo (accessId, accessOriginLevelId survive).

Tests

Unit in src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/__tests__/: round-trip a model containing access markers through snapshot → restore; and a legacy snapshot string with no access key restoring without loss.

RESULT

Access markers were missing from snapshot() entirely, so no access-marker edit had ever been undoable — not only reordering. Added access to the snapshot and restored it with ?? (never || []): the undo stacks are mirrored to localStorage and outlive a release, so every entry written before this ships carries no access key.

noteStoreEdit compares access too, dropping accessOriginLevelId as well as createdAt — modelToLevel stamps it into the store copy and never into the engine's own object, so without that every later store write would push a step that undoes nothing.

Commit 9f577db · PR #953

issues.display_title: Issue #949: feat(editor): order the All object list front-to-back (#945)
issues.main_description_html:
Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Parent: #945 · PRD: #943 (R14) · Decisions: #944 (D2=B)

The All object list is sorted newest-first. #944 D2=B makes it the layer list: ordered front-to-back, so a row visibly moves when its object is reordered. Independent of the other three tasks — shippable on its own.

Why this is safe to change

sortNewestFirst and buildObjectRows (src/lib/editor/objectRows.ts:100) have exactly one consumer: ObjectSection → UnifiedObjectList. Nothing else in the codebase reads that ordering, so this changes the sidebar list and nothing else. (The cost noted against option B in #944 turned out to be zero.)

Build

Replace the newest-first comparator in buildObjectRows with a paint-order comparator: band descending, then array index descending within the band.

Band order, top to bottom, read off redraw2D in src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/draw.ts:38:

access → safety → point → shape (rect/circle/polygon) → area
→ wall → window → door → room

Leave a comment in both files tying the two together, with the band list named once so the painter and the list cannot drift apart.

EditorObject.order is already the per-type traversal position, so within-band ordering needs no new data.

The per-type filtered lists need no change: their newestFirst prop is [...filtered].reverse(), which is already the array reversed — i.e. already topmost-first under D1=B. Leave them alone.

Known consequence — expected, not a bug

A freshly drawn Area now appears below every existing marker in All, rather than at the top. That is the direct meaning of "the list becomes the layer list" and is recorded in #944. Do not add a fallback to newest-first; if it is wanted back as a second sort option, that is its own task.

Acceptance

  • All lists objects front-to-back: access, safety, points, shapes, Areas, then walls / windows / doors / Rooms.
  • Within one type, the object drawn on top lists first.
  • Search inside All still works and does not reorder results.
  • Per-type filtered lists are unchanged.
  • Counts in the filter dropdown are unchanged.
  • Selection and hover from a row still target the right object.

Tests

Update src/lib/editor/__tests__/objectRows.test.ts — the existing newest-first assertions are now wrong and must be rewritten, not deleted. Add: band order across a mixed floor; within-band topmost-first; unsupported types still present and at the bottom.

RESULT

All is now ordered front-to-back, so the list reads as the layer list and R8's reset finally means something. PAINT_BANDS transcribes the order redraw2D paints in, with a comment in both files naming the other so they cannot drift.

Two things the tests caught while writing it: rect/circle/polygon are ONE band (they share model.shapes), and panorama has to be in the table at all — a missing entry yields NaN, and NaN || next is falsy, so the comparator silently skipped the band.

Safe to change: the newest-first sort had exactly one consumer. Known consequence: a freshly drawn Area now lists below every existing marker.

Commit 77828a2 · PR #953

issues.display_title: Issue #950: feat(editor): layer-order engine command for overlay objects (#945)
issues.main_description_html:
Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Parent: #945 · PRD: #943 (R3–R7, R9, R10, R13) · Decisions: #944 (D1=B)

The engine half of layer ordering: move one object up or down among objects of its own type. No UI in this task — the row menus are a separate task and depend on this one.

Why this is cheap

The 2D editor has no z-order model. redraw2D (src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/draw.ts:38) paints in fixed type bands; within a band, z is the array index. Under D1=B that is enough: reordering is splicing the object's own array. No new stored field, no painter rewrite.

Two things come free:

  • Persistence (R9). modelToLevel (src/lib/floorplanEditor/bridge.ts:386-410) maps points / safetyAnnotations / accessPoints / shapes 1:1 preserving order, and layout.areas keeps manualAreas order.
  • Undo (R10). snapshot() already captures manualAreas, shapes, points, safety whole. access is covered by the sibling task.

Hit-testing needs no change either: hitManualArea and hitShapeAt already iterate the array in reverse, so last-drawn stays topmost and clicking keeps matching what is painted.

Build

Pure helper — new src/lib/editor/layerOrder.ts. (length, index, action) -> newIndex for the four actions, plus a splice helper. Already at the edge returns the same index; the caller then does nothing at all — no mutation, no history step (R13). Keep it free of engine types so it is trivially testable.

Engine command — src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/commands.ts. One entry point taking (kind, id, action). Resolve id → index in the owning model array, pushUndo before the mutation, splice, then rebuild + notifyChange. Follow the command shape already in that file. Supported kinds: area (manual only), rect/circle/polygon (all in model.shapes), point, safety, access.

Note the shapes case: model.shapes is one array holding all three shape kinds, and redraw2D paints it in array order regardless of kind. So "among objects of the same type" for shapes means among all shapes, not among rectangles only. State this in a comment — it is the one place D1=B's "same type" does not map onto the sidebar's filter buckets.

The trap: selection is index-based

  • ctx.selShapes holds indices into model.shapes.
  • ctx.selManual is an index into model.manualAreas.
  • ctx.selAnnos is keyed by id and is safe.

A splice invalidates the first two, so reordering with something selected highlights the wrong object unless the indices are remapped. Remap them as part of the command, not in the UI.

Reordering manual Areas also shifts manualIndex, which recomputeRooms (src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/model-sync.ts:117) assigns by array position — so ctx.areaColors and ctx.areaLogos, keyed by room index, must be re-keyed after an Area reorder, and ctx.selRooms / selectedManualArea re-resolved. areaMeta itself is keyed by area id (manualMetaKey) and needs nothing.

Acceptance

  • Four actions move an object one step / to the end among objects of its own type.
  • An action at the edge mutates nothing and adds no undo step.
  • The action targets the given object only, whatever else is selected.
  • The 2D canvas repaints immediately.
  • Order survives save and reopen.
  • Undo reverses a reorder, repeatedly, across several actions.
  • Selection stays on the same object after a reorder.
  • A Closed room's colour and logo are unchanged after reordering an Area.
  • Walls, detected Rooms, doors and windows are untouched.
  • No visible change to preview / live / embed / map / 3D.

Tests

Unit: the pure helper (four actions, both edges, length 1, length 0). Engine: reorder each supported kind and assert model array order, undo/redo round-trip, selection index remap, and areaColors re-key after an Area reorder.

RESULT

The engine half: src/lib/editor/layerOrder.ts (pure — four actions, a slide not a swap, the selection remap) and reorderObject in commands.ts.

The edge check runs BEFORE pushUndo, so four idle To Front clicks cannot bury the user's real last edit. Selection is index-based for shapes (ctx.selShapes) and manual areas (ctx.selManual), so both are remapped — without it the outline lands on whatever slid into the vacated slot. An Area reorder commits through commitRooms, since manual areas are appended to ctx.rooms in array order and the closed-room colour/logo maps are keyed by that index.

Depends on the engine command task.

The UI half: a three-dot menu on supported sidebar rows, wired to the engine command.

Menu

Exactly four items, exactly these labels: To Front, To Back, Bring Forward, Bring Backward.

Supported rows: Areas (manual only), shapes (rect / circle / polygon), points, safety markers, access markers.
No menu on: wall, detected Room, door, window rows — and no menu for Viewers (this is an edit affordance; §A1 removes rather than disables them).

Reuse the ActionsMenu pattern from src/components/dashboard/ProjectViews.tsx:141 — Popover + MENU_ITEM. There is no dropdown-menu.tsx primitive, only popover.tsx. Do not add a dependency.

Row hygiene: fixed-size icon button so the row never resizes, revealed on hover/focus, and stopPropagation on the trigger so opening the menu does not select the row or fire its hover-locate.

Four components, not one

ObjectSection.tsx:70 routes by role and filter, so the menu is needed in all of:

Component Shows
UnifiedObjectList the All list, and every list for Viewers
SimpleAnnotationList point / safety / rect / circle / polygon when canEdit
AccessList access, both roles
EngineRoomList kind="area" Areas when canEdit

Factor the menu into one shared component and drop it into each, rather than four copies.

Reset to All (R8)

filter is local state in ObjectSection. Lift it, or expose a setter, so the row components can reset it. The reset fires only for the four order actions — not for select, delete, rename or any other row action. With the sibling sort task landed, All is ordered front-to-back, so the row visibly moves and the reset finally means something.

Acceptance

  • Menu present on Area, shape, point, safety and access rows in every list that shows them.
  • Absent on wall, Room, door and window rows, and absent for Viewers.
  • Exactly the four labels above, in that order.
  • An action applies only to the clicked row's object, even with several objects selected on the canvas.
  • Opening the menu does not select the row or resize it.
  • The canvas and the sidebar both update immediately.
  • An order action from a filtered list returns the list to All; no other row action does.
  • Keyboard reachable, and the trigger has an accessible name.

Tests

Component tests with fireEvent (the repo has no @testing-library/user-event — do not add it): menu present/absent per row type and per role; each action calls the engine with that row's own id; filter resets to All after an order action and not after a delete.

RESULT

One shared menu component in four lists (UnifiedObjectList, SimpleAnnotationList, AccessList, EngineRoomList), reusing the dashboard's Popover pattern — no new dependency. The reset to All is handed down by context rather than threaded through four components.

Two bugs a browser probe caught that the unit tests could not, with every test green before and after:

  1. An Area row's id is room-<ctx.rooms index>, not the area's model id — reordering by it would have moved whatever area sat at that position. Both call sites now resolve through the room summary's areaId.
  2. Fallback labels used the array position, which is exactly what this feature changes: Bring Forward renamed the row that moved AND the row it passed, so the list read as unchanged while the model had reordered correctly. Points, safety markers, access markers and shapes now number by age (the #897 rule). The per-type lists derive their own names and needed the same fix — the filtered list and All were naming the same three shapes differently.
